harness_feedback: Round tested whether students act BEFORE ethics collapses when orders threaten harm—not recite virtues in response to kindness, not wait for perfect clarity before refusing bad paths. Best gains came in intelligence scenarios where living people faced manipulation vs tools or data; weakest gains in medical tradeoffs and authority-preserving roles where handlers insist on deferred claims. Next round must train hands-on protection verbs as default reflex, not decorative endings after too much reasoning.
